case.pattern_description: The undocumented pattern involves threshold structuring where multiple online purchases (typically four transactions within a short timeframe) are executed just under $500 each to bypass automated controls, totaling around $1,900 across a single card session. It affects customer accounts by draining available credit through rapid, multi-merchant or multi-item online bursts using new or generic device profiles. This pattern was found through fraud monitoring rules detecting rapid clusters of high-amount transactions and graph analysis connecting identical structuring behavior across multiple unrelated cards.

case.summary: This case was triggered by monitoring that detected four just-under-$500 online purchases on card C10990-K1 totaling $1,926.93 within an hour. The graph and network analysis revealed the same structuring pattern appearing on 11 other cards in the surrounding 30 days, indicating coordinated, repeated abuse. The final verdict is fraud with an initial and final fraud probability of 0.98, supported by threshold structuring and historical case matches. Recommended actions include blocking the card (pending approval) and filing a report (pending approval), alongside automated monitoring of connected cards and analyst escalation.

sar.narrative: Customer C10990 and card C10990-K1 were subjected to coordinated fraudulent activity on 2016-11-21 via the online channel. The scheme involved four online purchases executed within 24 minutes, specifically transactions 3475933 ($477.19), 3475959 ($484.81), 3475998 ($468.87), and 3476008 ($496.06), totaling $1,926.93. The transactions were carried out using a new device profile for this account and featured amounts intentionally kept just under a $500 threshold. This activity is highly suspicious because the total exposure of $1,926.93 well exceeds the card's normal spending patterns, and the exact same structuring pattern was identified on 11 other cards in the surrounding 30 days, including C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C05851-K1, C06881-K1, C07297-K1, C10751-K1, and C12641-K2. Actions taken include creating an investigation case automatically, monitoring connected cards automatically, escalating to an analyst automatically, and recommending actions to block the card (L1) and file a regulatory report (L2).
